ko.title: 또 다시 마감일: 트럼프가 방금 연장한 90일간의 중국 관세 휴전의 내막

segments.src: ## The Can Gets Kicked Down the Road — Again
segments.tr: ## 다시 한번 미뤄진 문제

segments.src: For the third time in roughly a year, Washington and Beijing have stepped back from the edge of a full-blown tariff spike.
segments.tr: 약 1년 만에 세 번째로, 워싱턴과 베이징은 전면적인 관세 인상이라는 벼랑 끝에서 물러났습니다.

segments.src: Rather than allow the reciprocal tariff rate on Chinese goods to snap up toward the 125 percent level that had been threatened, the Trump administration agreed to push the deadline back another 90 days.
segments.tr: 트럼프 행정부는 중국 상품에 대한 상호 관세율이 위협했던 125% 수준으로 급등하는 것을 허용하는 대신, 마감일을 다시 90일 연장하는 데 동의했습니다.

segments.src: It is a familiar pattern by now: a looming cutoff, last-minute talks, and a truce that buys both sides more time without resolving much of anything.
segments.tr: 이제는 익숙한 패턴입니다. 임박한 마감일, 막판 협상, 그리고 많은 것을 해결하지 못한 채 양측에 시간을 벌어주는 휴전입니다.

segments.src: For businesses that import from China, for American consumers watching prices at the checkout counter, and for markets that have grown accustomed to tariff headlines, the extension is a relief.
segments.tr: 중국에서 수입하는 기업들, 계산대 앞의 가격을 지켜보는 미국 소비자들, 그리고 관세 관련 헤드라인에 익숙해진 시장들에게 이번 연장은 안도감을 줍니다.

segments.src: But it is also a reminder that the underlying dispute — over trade imbalances, technology restrictions, industrial subsidies, and market access — remains unsettled.
segments.tr: 하지만 이는 무역 불균형, 기술 제한, 산업 보조금 및 시장 접근성이라는 근본적인 분쟁이 여전히 해결되지 않은 채 남아 있음을 상기시킵니다.

segments.src: ## Why Neither Side Wants to Pull the Trigger
segments.tr: ## 양측 모두 방아쇠를 당기지 않으려는 이유

segments.src: Trade analysts have repeatedly pointed out that a jump to triple-digit tariffs would be disruptive for both economies, not just one.
segments.tr: 무역 분석가들은 관세가 세 자릿수로 급증하면 어느 한 쪽이 아니라 양국 경제 모두에 혼란을 초래할 것이라고 반복해서 지적해 왔습니다.

segments.src: U.S.
segments.tr: 미국의

segments.src: importers of electronics, machinery parts, and consumer goods would face sharply higher costs, much of which tends to be passed on to shoppers.
segments.tr: 전자제품, 기계 부품 및 소비재 수입업체들은 훨씬 더 높은 비용에 직면하게 될 것이며, 이 중 상당 부분은 소비자에게 전가되는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: Chinese exporters, meanwhile, would see a key market effectively close off overnight, adding pressure to an economy already dealing with soft domestic demand and a cooling property sector.
segments.tr: 한편, 중국 수출업체들은 핵심 시장이 하룻밤 사이에 사실상 폐쇄되는 것을 보게 될 것이며, 이는 이미 내수 부진과 부동산 부문 침체로 어려움을 겪고 있는 경제에 압박을 더할 것입니다.

segments.src: That mutual exposure appears to be the real force behind the repeated extensions.
segments.tr: 이러한 상호 노출이 반복적인 연장의 실제 동력으로 보입니다.

segments.src: Neither government wants to be blamed for reigniting a trade war that could rattle stock markets, spook manufacturers, and complicate other diplomatic priorities.
segments.tr: 어느 정부도 주식 시장을 흔들고, 제조업체를 겁먹게 하고, 다른 외교적 우선순위를 복잡하게 만들 수 있는 무역 전쟁을 다시 점화시키는 것에 대해 비난받고 싶어 하지 않습니다.

segments.src: A rolling 90-day truce lets both sides claim they are being tough while avoiding the economic shock a full tariff escalation would bring.
segments.tr: 90일마다 반복되는 휴전은 양측이 경제적 충격을 피하면서도 강경한 태도를 유지하고 있다고 주장할 수 있게 해줍니다.

segments.src: ## What a 90-Day Truce Actually Buys
segments.tr: ## 90일 휴전이 실제로 벌어주는 것

segments.src: A three-month extension is not a resolution — it is a pause button.
segments.tr: 3개월의 연장은 해결책이 아니라 일시 정지 버튼입니다.

segments.src: Typically, these windows are used for:
segments.tr: 일반적으로 이러한 기간은 다음과 같은 용도로 사용됩니다:

segments.src: - **Continued negotiations** on issues like agricultural purchases, technology export controls, and intellectual property enforcement
segments.tr: - **농산물 구매, 기술 수출 통제 및 지적 재산권 집행**과 같은 문제에 대한 지속적인 협상

segments.src: - **Business planning breathing room**, giving companies time to adjust supply chains rather than absorb sudden cost shocks
segments.tr: - **기업 계획의 숨통을 틔워주는 것**, 기업들이 갑작스러운 비용 충격을 흡수하는 대신 공급망을 조정할 시간을 주는 것

segments.src: - **Political cover**, allowing officials on both sides to point to "progress" without committing to a final deal
segments.tr: - **정치적 명분**, 양측 관리들이 최종 합의에 서명하지 않고도 "진전"이 있다고 주장할 수 있게 하는 것

segments.src: Critics of this approach argue that repeated short-term extensions create their own kind of uncertainty.
segments.tr: 이러한 접근 방식의 비판자들은 반복적인 단기 연장이 그 자체로 불확실성을 조성한다고 주장합니다.

segments.src: Companies that might otherwise invest in reshoring production or diversifying suppliers have less incentive to make permanent changes if there's a chance the tariff threat will simply be extended again.
segments.tr: 생산 시설의 리쇼어링이나 공급처 다변화를 고려하던 기업들은 관세 위협이 단순히 다시 연장될 가능성이 있다면 영구적인 변화를 시도할 동기가 줄어듭니다.

segments.src: Supporters counter that gradual, incremental de-escalation is preferable to an abrupt shock that could hit growth on both sides of the Pacific.
segments.tr: 지지자들은 태평양 양단에서 성장을 저해할 수 있는 갑작스러운 충격보다는 점진적이고 단계적인 긴장 완화가 더 바람직하다고 반박합니다.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## 다음으로 주목해야 할 점

segments.src: A few signals tend to matter most as each deadline approaches:
segments.tr: 마감일이 다가올 때마다 다음과 같은 몇 가지 신호가 가장 중요하게 작용하는 경향이 있습니다:

segments.src: 1. **Statements from trade representatives** on both sides about the tone of ongoing talks
segments.tr: 1. **양측 무역 대표들의 성명**, 현재 진행 중인 협상의 분위기에 관한 것

segments.src: 2. **Movement on non-tariff issues**, such as export licensing for semiconductors or restrictions on rare earth materials
segments.tr: 2. **비관세 문제의 움직임**, 반도체 수출 라이선스나 희토류 소재 제한과 같은 것

segments.src: 3. **Market reaction**, since equities and currency markets often price in expectations of either a deal or an escalation well before the deadline itself
segments.tr: 3. **시장 반응**, 주식 및 외환 시장은 종종 마감일 이전에 합의 또는 갈등 고조에 대한 기대치를 가격에 반영하기 때문입니다

segments.src: 4. **Whether this extension comes with any new conditions**, since some truces have included specific commitments — like purchase targets or enforcement mechanisms — while others have simply reset the clock
segments.tr: 4. **이번 연장에 새로운 조건이 붙었는지 여부**, 일부 휴전은 구매 목표나 집행 메커니즘과 같은 구체적인 약속을 포함했지만, 다른 휴전은 단순히 시간을 다시 설정했을 뿐이기 때문입니다

segments.src: ## The Bigger Picture
segments.tr: ## 더 큰 그림

segments.src: Whatever happens at the next deadline, the broader U.S.-China trade relationship has settled into a rhythm of managed tension rather than either full cooperation or open conflict.
segments.tr: 다음 마감일에 어떤 일이 일어나든, 더 넓은 의미의 미-중 무역 관계는 완전한 협력이나 공개적인 갈등보다는 관리된 긴장 상태의 리듬으로 자리 잡았습니다.

segments.src: Tariff truces like this one don't erase the disagreements that triggered them in the first place — they just delay the moment when one side has to decide whether to escalate or fold.
segments.tr: 이와 같은 관세 휴전은 처음에 그것을 유발한 불일치를 지우지 않습니다. 단지 한 쪽이 갈등을 고조시키거나 굴복해야 하는 순간을 늦출 뿐입니다.

segments.src: For now, the 90-day extension keeps supply chains intact, keeps price increases from hitting all at once, and keeps the door open for further talks.
segments.tr: 현재로서는 90일 연장이 공급망을 유지하고, 가격 인상이 한꺼번에 닥치는 것을 막으며, 추가 협상의 문을 열어둡니다.

segments.src: Whether it leads anywhere more permanent likely won't be clear until the next deadline comes into view.
segments.tr: 이것이 더 영구적인 결과로 이어질지는 다음 마감일이 보이기 시작할 때까지는 분명하지 않을 것입니다.

zh.title: 再次延期：特朗普刚刚延长 90 天中国关税休战期的内幕

segments.src: ## The Can Gets Kicked Down the Road — Again
segments.tr: ## 问题再次被推迟

segments.src: For the third time in roughly a year, Washington and Beijing have stepped back from the edge of a full-blown tariff spike.
segments.tr: 在大约一年的时间里，华盛顿和北京第三次从全面关税飙升的边缘退回。

segments.src: Rather than allow the reciprocal tariff rate on Chinese goods to snap up toward the 125 percent level that had been threatened, the Trump administration agreed to push the deadline back another 90 days.
segments.tr: 特朗普政府同意将截止日期再推迟 90 天，而不是让中国商品的互惠关税税率飙升至此前威胁的 125% 水平。

segments.src: It is a familiar pattern by now: a looming cutoff, last-minute talks, and a truce that buys both sides more time without resolving much of anything.
segments.tr: 这已经成了一个熟悉的模式：临近截止日期，最后一刻的谈判，以及一个在没有解决任何实质性问题的情况下为双方赢得更多时间的休战期。

segments.src: For businesses that import from China, for American consumers watching prices at the checkout counter, and for markets that have grown accustomed to tariff headlines, the extension is a relief.
segments.tr: 对于从中国进口的企业、关注结账柜台价格的美国消费者，以及已经习惯了关税头条新闻的市场来说，这次延期是一个宽慰。

segments.src: But it is also a reminder that the underlying dispute — over trade imbalances, technology restrictions, industrial subsidies, and market access — remains unsettled.
segments.tr: 但这也提醒人们，潜在的争端——关于贸易失衡、技术限制、工业补贴和市场准入——仍然没有解决。

segments.src: ## Why Neither Side Wants to Pull the Trigger
segments.tr: ## 为什么双方都不想扣动扳机

segments.src: Trade analysts have repeatedly pointed out that a jump to triple-digit tariffs would be disruptive for both economies, not just one.
segments.tr: 贸易分析师多次指出，关税跃升至三位数将对两国经济产生破坏性影响，而不仅仅是一方。

segments.src: U.S.
segments.tr: 美国的

segments.src: importers of electronics, machinery parts, and consumer goods would face sharply higher costs, much of which tends to be passed on to shoppers.
segments.tr: 电子产品、机械零件和消费品的进口商将面临大幅提高的成本，其中大部分往往会转嫁给购物者。

segments.src: Chinese exporters, meanwhile, would see a key market effectively close off overnight, adding pressure to an economy already dealing with soft domestic demand and a cooling property sector.
segments.tr: 与此同时，中国出口商将看到一个关键市场在一夜之间实际上关闭，这给已经面临国内需求疲软和房地产行业冷却的经济增加了压力。

segments.src: That mutual exposure appears to be the real force behind the repeated extensions.
segments.tr: 这种相互牵制似乎是重复延期的真实动力。

segments.src: Neither government wants to be blamed for reigniting a trade war that could rattle stock markets, spook manufacturers, and complicate other diplomatic priorities.
segments.tr: 没有任何一个政府希望被指责为重新点燃贸易战，因为这可能会动摇股市，惊吓制造商，并使其他外交优先级复杂化。

segments.src: A rolling 90-day truce lets both sides claim they are being tough while avoiding the economic shock a full tariff escalation would bring.
segments.tr: 滚动式的 90 天休战让双方在避免全面关税升级带来的经济冲击的同时，可以声称自己态度强硬。

segments.src: ## What a 90-Day Truce Actually Buys
segments.tr: ## 90 天休战期实际上带来了什么

segments.src: A three-month extension is not a resolution — it is a pause button.
segments.tr: 三个月的延期并不是解决方案——而是一个暂停键。

segments.src: Typically, these windows are used for:
segments.tr: 通常，这些窗口期被用于：

segments.src: - **Continued negotiations** on issues like agricultural purchases, technology export controls, and intellectual property enforcement
segments.tr: - **就农产品采购、技术出口管制和知识产权执法等问题继续谈判**

segments.src: - **Business planning breathing room**, giving companies time to adjust supply chains rather than absorb sudden cost shocks
segments.tr: - **给企业规划提供喘息空间**，让公司有时间调整供应链，而不是吸收突然的成本冲击

segments.src: - **Political cover**, allowing officials on both sides to point to "progress" without committing to a final deal
segments.tr: - **政治掩护**，允许双方官员在不承诺最终协议的情况下指出“进展”

segments.src: Critics of this approach argue that repeated short-term extensions create their own kind of uncertainty.
segments.tr: 这种方法的批评者认为，重复的短期延期创造了其自身的某种不确定性。

segments.src: Companies that might otherwise invest in reshoring production or diversifying suppliers have less incentive to make permanent changes if there's a chance the tariff threat will simply be extended again.
segments.tr: 如果关税威胁可能再次被简单地延期，那么原本可能投资于生产回流或供应商多样化的公司，进行永久性改变的动力就会降低。

segments.src: Supporters counter that gradual, incremental de-escalation is preferable to an abrupt shock that could hit growth on both sides of the Pacific.
segments.tr: 支持者则反驳说，渐进式的去升级比可能打击太平洋两岸增长的突然冲击更可取。

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## 接下来关注什么

segments.src: A few signals tend to matter most as each deadline approaches:
segments.tr: 随着每个截止日期的临近，几个信号往往最为重要：

segments.src: 1. **Statements from trade representatives** on both sides about the tone of ongoing talks
segments.tr: 1. **双方贸易代表关于正在进行的谈判基调的声明**

segments.src: 2. **Movement on non-tariff issues**, such as export licensing for semiconductors or restrictions on rare earth materials
segments.tr: 2. **非关税问题的进展**，例如半导体出口许可或稀土材料限制

segments.src: 3. **Market reaction**, since equities and currency markets often price in expectations of either a deal or an escalation well before the deadline itself
segments.tr: 3. **市场反应**，因为股票和货币市场通常在截止日期之前很久就将协议或升级的预期计入价格

segments.src: 4. **Whether this extension comes with any new conditions**, since some truces have included specific commitments — like purchase targets or enforcement mechanisms — while others have simply reset the clock
segments.tr: 4. **这次延期是否带有任何新条件**，因为有些休战包括具体承诺——如采购目标或执行机制——而有些则仅仅是重新设定时钟

segments.src: ## The Bigger Picture
segments.tr: ## 更宏观的视角

segments.src: Whatever happens at the next deadline, the broader U.S.-China trade relationship has settled into a rhythm of managed tension rather than either full cooperation or open conflict.
segments.tr: 无论下一个截止日期发生什么，更广泛的美中贸易关系已经进入了一种管理紧张状态的节奏，而不是完全合作或公开冲突。

segments.src: Tariff truces like this one don't erase the disagreements that triggered them in the first place — they just delay the moment when one side has to decide whether to escalate or fold.
segments.tr: 像这样的关税休战并不能消除最初引发它们的分歧——它们只是推迟了其中一方必须决定是升级还是让步的时刻。

segments.src: For now, the 90-day extension keeps supply chains intact, keeps price increases from hitting all at once, and keeps the door open for further talks.
segments.tr: 目前，90 天的延期保持了供应链的完整，防止了价格上涨一次性冲击，并为进一步谈判留开了大门。

segments.src: Whether it leads anywhere more permanent likely won't be clear until the next deadline comes into view.

hi.title: एक समय सीमा, फिर से: ट्रम्प द्वारा विस्तारित 90-दिवसीय चीन टैरिफ युद्धविराम के अंदर

segments.src: ## The Can Gets Kicked Down the Road — Again
segments.tr: ## मामला फिर से टाल दिया गया — एक बार फिर

segments.src: For the third time in roughly a year, Washington and Beijing have stepped back from the edge of a full-blown tariff spike.
segments.tr: लगभग एक वर्ष में तीसरी बार, वाशिंगटन और बीजिंग एक पूर्ण टैरिफ वृद्धि के कगार से पीछे हट गए हैं।

segments.src: Rather than allow the reciprocal tariff rate on Chinese goods to snap up toward the 125 percent level that had been threatened, the Trump administration agreed to push the deadline back another 90 days.
segments.tr: चीनी सामानों पर पारस्परिक टैरिफ दर को उस 125 प्रतिशत स्तर तक पहुँचने देने के बजाय जिसकी धमकी दी गई थी, ट्रम्प प्रशासन ने समय सीमा को और 90 दिनों के लिए आगे बढ़ाने पर सहमति व्यक्त की।

segments.src: Chinese exporters, meanwhile, would see a key market effectively close off overnight, adding pressure to an economy already dealing with soft domestic demand and a cooling property sector.
segments.tr: वहीं, चीनी निर्यातकों को एक प्रमुख बाजार प्रभावी रूप से रातों-रात बंद होता हुआ दिखेगा, जिससे पहले से ही कमजोर घरेलू मांग और ठंडे पड़ते प्रॉपर्टी सेक्टर की समस्या से जूझ रही अर्थव्यवस्था पर दबाव बढ़ेगा।

segments.src: Neither government wants to be blamed for reigniting a trade war that could rattle stock markets, spook manufacturers, and complicate other diplomatic priorities.

segments.src: Typically, these windows are used for:

segments.src: - **Business planning breathing room**, giving companies time to adjust supply chains rather than absorb sudden cost shocks

segments.src: - **Political cover**, allowing officials on both sides to point to "progress" without committing to a final deal
segments.tr: - **राजनीतिक कवर**, जिससे दोनों पक्षों के अधिकारियों को अंतिम समझौते पर प्रतिबद्ध होने के बिना "प्रगति" की ओर इशारा करने की अनुमति मिले

segments.src: Critics of this approach argue that repeated short-term extensions create their own kind of uncertainty.
segments.tr: इस दृष्टिकोण के आलोचकों का तर्क है कि बार-बार होने वाले अल्पकालिक विस्तार अपनी स्वयं की अनिश्चितता पैदा करते हैं।

segments.src: Companies that might otherwise invest in reshoring production or diversifying suppliers have less incentive to make permanent changes if there's a chance the tariff threat will simply be extended again.

segments.src: Supporters counter that gradual, incremental de-escalation is preferable to an abrupt shock that could hit growth on both sides of the Pacific.
segments.tr: समर्थकों का तर्क है कि प्रशांत महासागर के दोनों ओर विकास पर प्रहार करने वाले अचानक झटके की तुलना में धीरे-धीरे, क्रमिक वि-उत्तेजना (de-escalation) अधिक पसंद योग्य है।

es.title: Un plazo más, otra vez: Dentro de la tregua arancelaria de 90 días con China que Trump acaba de extender

segments.src: ## The Can Gets Kicked Down the Road — Again
segments.tr: ## El problema se pospone — una vez más

segments.src: For the third time in roughly a year, Washington and Beijing have stepped back from the edge of a full-blown tariff spike.
segments.tr: Por tercera vez en aproximadamente un año, Washington y Pekín se han alejado del borde de un aumento arancelario total.

segments.src: Rather than allow the reciprocal tariff rate on Chinese goods to snap up toward the 125 percent level that had been threatened, the Trump administration agreed to push the deadline back another 90 days.
segments.tr: En lugar de permitir que la tasa arancelaria recíproca sobre los productos chinos subiera hacia el nivel del 125 por ciento que se había amenazado, la administración Trump acordó retrasar la fecha límite otros 90 días.

segments.src: It is a familiar pattern by now: a looming cutoff, last-minute talks, and a truce that buys both sides more time without resolving much of anything.
segments.tr: Es un patrón familiar a estas alturas: un plazo límite inminente, conversaciones de último minuto y una tregua que otorga a ambas partes más tiempo sin resolver gran parte de nada.

segments.src: For businesses that import from China, for American consumers watching prices at the checkout counter, and for markets that have grown accustomed to tariff headlines, the extension is a relief.
segments.tr: Para las empresas que importan de China, para los consumidores estadounidenses que observan los precios en la caja, y para los mercados que se han acostumbrado a los titulares sobre aranceles, la extensión es un alivio.

segments.src: But it is also a reminder that the underlying dispute — over trade imbalances, technology restrictions, industrial subsidies, and market access — remains unsettled.
segments.tr: Pero también es un recordatorio de que la disputa subyacente — sobre desequilibrios comerciales, restricciones tecnológicas, subsidios industriales y acceso al mercado — sigue sin resolverse.

segments.tr: ## Por qué ninguna de las partes quiere apretar el gatillo

segments.tr: Los analistas comerciales han señalado repetidamente que un salto a aranceles de tres dígitos sería disruptivo para ambas economías, no solo para una.

fr.title: Un nouveau délai : Dans les coulisses de la trêve tarifaire de 90 jours avec la Chine que Trump vient de prolonger

segments.src: ## The Can Gets Kicked Down the Road — Again

segments.src: For the third time in roughly a year, Washington and Beijing have stepped back from the edge of a full-blown tariff spike.
segments.tr: Pour la troisième fois en environ un an, Washington et Pékin se sont éloignés du bord d'une hausse massive des tarifs douaniers.

segments.src: Rather than allow the reciprocal tariff rate on Chinese goods to snap up toward the 125 percent level that had been threatened, the Trump administration agreed to push the deadline back another 90 days.
segments.tr: Plutôt que de laisser le taux tarifaire réciproque sur les marchandises chinoises grimper vers le niveau de 125 % qui avait été menacé, l'administration Trump a accepté de repousser l'échéance de 90 jours supplémentaires.

segments.src: It is a familiar pattern by now: a looming cutoff, last-minute talks, and a truce that buys both sides more time without resolving much of anything.
segments.tr: C'est un schéma familier désormais : une date limite imminente, des discussions de dernière minute et une trêve qui donne plus de temps aux deux parties sans pour autant résoudre grand-chose.

segments.src: For businesses that import from China, for American consumers watching prices at the checkout counter, and for markets that have grown accustomed to tariff headlines, the extension is a relief.
segments.tr: Pour les entreprises qui importent de Chine, pour les consommateurs américains qui surveillent les prix à la caisse, et pour les marchés qui se sont habitués aux gros titres sur les tarifs, cette prolongation est un soulagement.

segments.src: But it is also a reminder that the underlying dispute — over trade imbalances, technology restrictions, industrial subsidies, and market access — remains unsettled.
segments.tr: Mais c'est aussi un rappel que le différend sous-jacent — portant sur les déséquilibres commerciaux, les restrictions technologiques, les subventions industrielles et l'accès au marché — reste non résolu.

segments.src: ## Why Neither Side Wants to Pull the Trigger
segments.tr: ## Pourquoi aucune des deux parties ne veut appuyer sur la gâchette

segments.src: Trade analysts have repeatedly pointed out that a jump to triple-digit tariffs would be disruptive for both economies, not just one.
segments.tr: Les analystes commerciaux ont souligné à plusieurs reprises qu'un bond vers des tarifs à trois chiffres serait perturbateur pour les deux économies, et pas seulement pour l'une d'elles.

segments.src: Chinese exporters, meanwhile, would see a key market effectively close off overnight, adding pressure to an economy already dealing with soft domestic demand and a cooling property sector.

segments.tr: Une trêve glissante de 90 jours permet aux deux parties de prétendre être fermes tout en évitant le choc économique qu'apporterait une escalade tarifaire complète.

segments.src: ## What a 90-Day Truce Actually Buys
segments.tr: ## Ce qu'une trêve de 90 jours permet réellement d'obtenir

segments.tr: Une prolongation de trois mois n'est pas une résolution — c'est un bouton pause.

segments.src: - **Business planning breathing room**, giving companies time to adjust supply chains rather than absorb sudden cost shocks
segments.tr: - **Un répit pour la planification des entreprises**, donnant aux sociétés le temps d'ajuster les chaînes d'approvisionnement plutôt que d'absorber des chocs de coûts soudains

segments.src: - **Political cover**, allowing officials on both sides to point to "progress" without committing to a final deal
segments.tr: - **Une couverture politique**, permettant aux responsables des deux parties de pointer un "progrès" sans s'engager dans un accord final

segments.src: Critics of this approach argue that repeated short-term extensions create their own kind of uncertainty.

segments.src: Companies that might otherwise invest in reshoring production or diversifying suppliers have less incentive to make permanent changes if there's a chance the tariff threat will simply be extended again.

segments.tr: Untuk ketiga kalinya dalam waktu sekitar satu tahun, Washington dan Beijing telah mundur dari ambang lonjakan tarif besar-besaran.

segments.src: Rather than allow the reciprocal tariff rate on Chinese goods to snap up toward the 125 percent level that had been threatened, the Trump administration agreed to push the deadline back another 90 days.
segments.tr: Alih-alih membiarkan tarif timbal balik atas barang-barang China melonjak ke level 125 persen yang telah diancamkan, pemerintahan Trump setuju untuk memundurkan tenggat waktu selama 90 hari lagi.

segments.src: It is a familiar pattern by now: a looming cutoff, last-minute talks, and a truce that buys both sides more time without resolving much of anything.
segments.tr: Ini adalah pola yang sudah lazim sekarang: tenggat waktu yang mendekat, pembicaraan menit terakhir, dan gencatan senjata yang memberi kedua belah pihak lebih banyak waktu tanpa menyelesaikan banyak hal.

segments.src: For businesses that import from China, for American consumers watching prices at the checkout counter, and for markets that have grown accustomed to tariff headlines, the extension is a relief.
segments.tr: Bagi bisnis yang mengimpor dari China, bagi konsumen Amerika yang memantau harga di kasir, dan bagi pasar yang telah terbiasa dengan berita utama tentang tarif, perpanjangan ini merupakan sebuah kelegaan.

segments.src: But it is also a reminder that the underlying dispute — over trade imbalances, technology restrictions, industrial subsidies, and market access — remains unsettled.
segments.tr: Namun, ini juga menjadi pengingat bahwa perselisihan mendasar — mengenai ketidakseimbangan perdagangan, pembatasan teknologi, subsidi industri, dan akses pasar — tetap belum terselesaikan.

segments.src: ## Why Neither Side Wants to Pull the Trigger

de.title: Wieder eine Frist: Ein Blick hinter die 90-Tage-Zollruhe zwischen den USA und China, die Trump gerade verlängert hat

segments.src: ## The Can Gets Kicked Down the Road — Again
segments.tr: ## Die Sache wird erneut aufgeschoben

segments.src: For the third time in roughly a year, Washington and Beijing have stepped back from the edge of a full-blown tariff spike.
segments.tr: Zum dritten Mal innerhalb eines Jahres sind Washington und Peking vom Rande einer massiven Zollsteigerung zurückgetreten.

segments.src: Rather than allow the reciprocal tariff rate on Chinese goods to snap up toward the 125 percent level that had been threatened, the Trump administration agreed to push the deadline back another 90 days.
segments.tr: Anstatt zuzulassen, dass der gegenseitige Zollsatz für chinesische Waren auf das angedrohte Niveau von 125 Prozent ansteigt, stimmte die Trump-Administration zu, die Frist um weitere 90 Tage zu verlängern.

segments.src: It is a familiar pattern by now: a looming cutoff, last-minute talks, and a truce that buys both sides more time without resolving much of anything.
segments.tr: Es ist mittlerweile ein bekanntes Muster: eine drohende Deadline, Gespräche in letzter Minute und ein Waffenstillstand, der beiden Seiten mehr Zeit verschafft, ohne vieles zu lösen.

segments.src: For businesses that import from China, for American consumers watching prices at the checkout counter, and for markets that have grown accustomed to tariff headlines, the extension is a relief.
segments.tr: Für Unternehmen, die aus China importieren, für amerikanische Verbraucher, die die Preise an der Kasse beobachten, und für Märkte, die sich an Zoll-Schlagzeilen gewöhnt haben, ist die Verlängerung eine Erleichterung.

segments.src: But it is also a reminder that the underlying dispute — over trade imbalances, technology restrictions, industrial subsidies, and market access — remains unsettled.
segments.tr: Aber sie ist auch eine Erinnerung daran, dass der zugrunde liegende Streit – über Handelsungleichgewichte, Technologiebeschränkungen, Industriesubventionen und Marktzugang – ungeklärt bleibt.

segments.src: ## Why Neither Side Wants to Pull the Trigger
segments.tr: ## Warum keine Seite den Abzug drücken will

segments.src: Trade analysts have repeatedly pointed out that a jump to triple-digit tariffs would be disruptive for both economies, not just one.
segments.tr: Handelsanalysten haben wiederholt darauf hingewiesen, dass ein Sprung in den dreistelligen Zollbereich für beide Volkswirtschaften disruptiv wäre, nicht nur für eine.

segments.src: U.S.
segments.tr: US-

segments.src: importers of electronics, machinery parts, and consumer goods would face sharply higher costs, much of which tends to be passed on to shoppers.
segments.tr: Importeure von Elektronik, Maschinenteilen und Konsumgütern stünden vor drastisch höheren Kosten, die zu einem großen Teil an die Käufer weitergegeben würden.

segments.src: Chinese exporters, meanwhile, would see a key market effectively close off overnight, adding pressure to an economy already dealing with soft domestic demand and a cooling property sector.
segments.tr: Chinesische Exporteure hingegen würden sehen, wie ein Schlüsselmarkt über Nacht effektiv geschlossen wird, was den Druck auf eine Wirtschaft erhöht, die bereits mit einer schwachen Binnennachfrage und einem abkühlenden Immobiliensektor zu kämpfen hat.

segments.src: That mutual exposure appears to be the real force behind the repeated extensions.
segments.tr: Diese gegenseitige Abhängigkeit scheint die eigentliche Kraft hinter den wiederholten Verlängerungen zu sein.

segments.src: Neither government wants to be blamed for reigniting a trade war that could rattle stock markets, spook manufacturers, and complicate other diplomatic priorities.
segments.tr: Keine der Regierungen möchte die Schuld dafür tragen, einen Handelskrieg neu zu entfachen, der die Aktienmärkte erschüttern, Hersteller verschrecken und andere diplomatische Prioritäten verkomplizieren könnte.

segments.src: A rolling 90-day truce lets both sides claim they are being tough while avoiding the economic shock a full tariff escalation would bring.
segments.tr: Ein rollierender 90-Tage-Waffenstillstand erlaubt es beiden Seiten, zu behaupten, sie seien hart, während sie den wirtschaftlichen Schock vermeiden, den eine vollständige Zolleskalation mit sich bringen würde.

segments.src: ## What a 90-Day Truce Actually Buys
segments.tr: ## Was ein 90-Tage-Waffenstillstand tatsächlich bringt

segments.src: A three-month extension is not a resolution — it is a pause button.
segments.tr: Eine dreimonatige Verlängerung ist keine Lösung – sie ist eine Pausentaste.

segments.src: Typically, these windows are used for:
segments.tr: Typischerweise werden diese Zeitfenster für Folgendes genutzt:

segments.src: - **Continued negotiations** on issues like agricultural purchases, technology export controls, and intellectual property enforcement
segments.tr: - **Fortgesetzte Verhandlungen** über Themen wie Agrarkäufe, Technologie-Exportkontrollen und die Durchsetzung von geistigem Eigentum

segments.src: - **Business planning breathing room**, giving companies time to adjust supply chains rather than absorb sudden cost shocks
segments.tr: - **Atempause für die Geschäftsplanung**, damit Unternehmen Zeit haben, Lieferketten anzupassen, anstatt plötzliche Kostenschocks zu absorbieren

segments.src: - **Political cover**, allowing officials on both sides to point to "progress" without committing to a final deal
segments.tr: - **Politische Deckung**, die es Beamten beider Seiten ermöglicht, auf "Fortschritte" hinzuweisen, ohne sich auf ein endgültiges Abkommen zu verpflichten

segments.src: Critics of this approach argue that repeated short-term extensions create their own kind of uncertainty.
segments.tr: Kritiker dieses Ansatzes argumentieren, dass wiederholte kurzfristige Verlängerungen ihre eigene Art von Unsicherheit schaffen.

segments.src: Companies that might otherwise invest in reshoring production or diversifying suppliers have less incentive to make permanent changes if there's a chance the tariff threat will simply be extended again.
segments.tr: Unternehmen, die ansonsten in das Reshoring der Produktion oder die Diversifizierung von Lieferanten investieren würden, haben weniger Anreize, dauerhafte Änderungen vorzunehmen, wenn die Chance besteht, dass die Zollbedrohung einfach erneut verlängert wird.

segments.src: Supporters counter that gradual, incremental de-escalation is preferable to an abrupt shock that could hit growth on both sides of the Pacific.
segments.tr: Befürworter halten dagegen, dass eine schrittweise, inkrementelle Deeskalation vorzuziehen ist als ein abrupter Schock, der das Wachstum auf beiden Seiten des Pazifiks treffen könnte.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## Worauf man als Nächstes achten sollte

segments.src: A few signals tend to matter most as each deadline approaches:
segments.tr: Einige Signale sind meist am wichtigsten, wenn jede Frist näher rückt:

segments.src: 1. **Statements from trade representatives** on both sides about the tone of ongoing talks
segments.tr: 1. **Erklärungen von Handelsvertretern** beider Seiten über den Ton der laufenden Gespräche

segments.src: 2. **Movement on non-tariff issues**, such as export licensing for semiconductors or restrictions on rare earth materials
segments.tr: 2. **Bewegungen bei nicht-tarifären Themen**, wie Exportlizenzen für Halbleiter oder Beschränkungen für Seltene Erden

segments.src: 3. **Market reaction**, since equities and currency markets often price in expectations of either a deal or an escalation well before the deadline itself
segments.tr: 3. **Marktreaktion**, da Aktien- und Währungsmärkte oft Erwartungen an ein Abkommen oder eine Eskalation lange vor der eigentlichen Frist einpreisen

segments.src: 4. **Whether this extension comes with any new conditions**, since some truces have included specific commitments — like purchase targets or enforcement mechanisms — while others have simply reset the clock
segments.tr: 4. **Ob diese Verlängerung mit neuen Bedingungen verbunden ist**, da einige Waffenstillstände spezifische Verpflichtungen – wie Kaufziele oder Durchsetzungsmechanismen – enthielten, während andere einfach die Uhr zurücksetzten

segments.src: ## The Bigger Picture
segments.tr: ## Das größere Bild

segments.src: Whatever happens at the next deadline, the broader U.S.-China trade relationship has settled into a rhythm of managed tension rather than either full cooperation or open conflict.
segments.tr: Was auch immer bei der nächsten Frist passiert, die breitere US-China-Handelsbeziehung hat sich in einen Rhythmus kontrollierter Spannung eingependelt, anstatt in eine vollständige Kooperation oder einen offenen Konflikt.

segments.src: Tariff truces like this one don't erase the disagreements that triggered them in the first place — they just delay the moment when one side has to decide whether to escalate or fold.
segments.tr: Zollwaffenstillstände wie dieser löschen nicht die Unstimmigkeiten aus, die sie ursprünglich ausgelöst haben – sie verzögern nur den Moment, wenn eine Seite entscheiden muss, ob sie eskaliert oder einknickt.

segments.src: For now, the 90-day extension keeps supply chains intact, keeps price increases from hitting all at once, and keeps the door open for further talks.
segments.tr: Fürs Erste hält die 90-Tage-Verlängerung die Lieferketten intakt, verhindert, dass Preiserhöhungen alle auf einmal treffen, und hält die Tür für weitere Gespräche offen.

segments.src: Whether it leads anywhere more permanent likely won't be clear until the next deadline comes into view.
segments.tr: Ob dies zu etwas Dauerhafterem führt, wird wahrscheinlich erst klar, wenn die nächste Frist in Sicht kommt.
